page.title: Proposals
page.purpose: Show promotions that agents have proposed and let an operator accept or decline with a reason. This is the only path by which an offer becomes active.

priorities.statement: What is being proposed, and by which actor
Declined history, so a repeated proposal is visible as repeated

states.description: The surface at rest with data present — the state a journey step assumes when it names none.
Nothing in flight; the surface is at rest and its controls are usable.
A user-triggered operation is in flight and its outcome is not yet known.
An operation completed; the result is announced, not merely rendered.
First read of the surface's data; layout is reserved so nothing shifts on arrival.
A write is in flight; the affected control is disabled and says why.
A background read is refreshing data the user is already looking at.
A user-requested re-read of data already on screen.
The query succeeded and there is genuinely nothing — distinct from not-yet-loaded.
Some contributing source could not be read; what is missing is named.
Displayed data is older than its freshness window; its age is shown.
Input was rejected before submission; the offending field is identified.
The request failed; the reason and the next action are stated.
An automatic retry is in progress; attempt count and next attempt are visible.
The caller's role does not permit this; what role would is stated.
The client cannot reach the API; queued or read-only behavior is explained.
A proposal exists and no operator has ruled on it; its age is shown because an old undisposed proposal is itself a signal.
An agent-authored proposal is present and its acceptance control states that only an operator may grant it.

elements.name: Proposals
elements.description: Open promotion proposals awaiting operator disposition.
Which actor authored the proposal, taken from the authenticated context rather than a request field.

elements.name: Evidence
elements.description: The facts and values the proposer read, so the operator can check the reasoning rather than trust it.
What accepting this proposal will change, stated before the accept control.

elements.name: Previously declined
elements.description: Prior declines for the same offer, so a repeated proposal is visible as repeated.
States that acceptance requires an operator role and that agents may only propose.

claims.statement: Every proposal states which actor authored it.
claims.rationale: Priority 1 and SECURITY.md. The operator's decision depends on who proposed it, and the identity must come from the authenticated context rather than a request field.

claims.statement: The evidence the proposer read appears before the accept control.
claims.rationale: Priorities 2 and 3. An accept control reachable before the reasoning invites rubber-stamping, which would make the operator boundary ceremonial.

claims.statement: The acceptance control states that granting requires an operator role and that agents may only propose.
claims.rationale: OT-P0-005. Making the boundary visible is what turns it from an implementation detail into a guarantee the operator can rely on.

claims.statement: Prior declines for the same offer are shown alongside a new proposal.
claims.rationale: Priority 4. Without decline history an agent can re-propose indefinitely and the operator re-decides from scratch each time.

claims.statement: What accepting will change is stated before the accept control.
claims.rationale: Promotion to active is the one irreversible-feeling action in the scenario; its consequence should never be inferred.

claims.statement: The acceptance control is operable from the keyboard.
claims.rationale: It is the operator's single most important action in the scenario.
